messages:
arjun: Pushing up an nsys trace from the 03:14 regressions. Noticeable queue-time spike correlated with a KV-cache sweep + prefetch event. attaching a short timeline excerpt.

arjun: ```
# nsys timeline snippet (filtered)
[0.000s] enqueue req id=824
[0.004s] kernel cutlass_gemm :: compute 0.8ms
[0.006s] KVCache::prefetch range(1024,2048) -> host memcpy 1.9ms
[0.008s] queue_delay id=825 4.2ms  <-- spike starts
[0.012s] kernel fused_attention_opt :: compute 2.1ms
[0.015s] kernel generic_attention_fallback :: compute 7.9ms  <-- kernel selection flip
[0.023s] completion id=824
```

arjun: TL;DR: small bursts (batch size 1-3) + prefetch leads to kernel fallback and a 3-8ms extra tail on some requests.

maya: Is this happening only when prefetch runs, or also on regular sweep?

arjun: Seems tied to prefetch + sweep timing. When KV sweep overlaps with the batch slicer window we see queue jitter. Sweep -> host memcpy -> GPU queue grows -> scheduler picks fallback kernel on some slices.

tom: That kernel flip smells like shape/padding differences. Batch-slicer occasionally produces very short sequences that hit a different kernel path. We should confirm by forcing constant batch sizing.

maya: Can you paste the exact profile command you used? I'll re-run with debug nvtx.

arjun: ```bash
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --capture-range=none --output=run_prefetch_03 
  --sample=cpu --force-overwrite -- 
  ./rinf_runtime --workload=serve --route=batch-slice-test --duration=30s
```

emily: I'll take the experiment. Plan: 3 variants A/B/C across the same seed traffic:
- A: baseline (current batch_slicer + prefetch)
- B: batch_slicer.min_slice=4 (avoid tiny slices)
- C: disable prefetch (kv.prefetch=false) + delay sweep to 50ms

emily: Need the image tag and the short repro script.

perf-bot: build #892 -> rinf/runtime:892 ✅ (artifacts: docker, debug-symbols).

luis: Also check host-side memcpy scheduling — last time we saw host memcpy contended with GPU driver worker threads and caused tail latency. Kernel names and host CPU runqueue look noisy in the trace.

tom: Good call. Add a perf stat on the host during runs: `perf stat -e cpu-migrations,context-switches -p $PID` and collect `dmesg`/`irq` times.

arjun: I attached a perfetto link with full trace (private): https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234

arjun: Early micro-obs from the trace: when queue_delay > 3ms, 72% of affected slices show `generic_attention_fallback`. When queue_delay < 1ms, fallback rate drops to <8%. Suggests the scheduler picks generic kernel under contention.

emily: Running A/B/C now on a small fleet (4 pods). Will share nsys + perfetto links when done. ETA ~25m.

maya: If B (larger min_slice) reduces fallback but hurts avg throughput, we might instead bias kernel selector to prefer the optimized path for small slices for a short window. i.e., add a 2-4ms grace where we avoid switching kernels if the selector sees frequent repeated shapes.

tom: That grace sounds promising and low-risk. Also consider making KV-cache sweep jittered (randomized offset) so it doesn't align to batch windows.

emily: Noted. I'll include a variant D: baseline + kernel-selector-delay=3ms + jittered-sweep.

arjun: Action items: 
- emily: run A/B/C/D and post traces (nsys + perfetto) + per-route p50/p95 tokens/latency.
- tom: add perf counters to the kernel selector to log when it flips and why (padding vs mem-bound).
- maya: prototype kernel-selector-delay heuristic and a small unit-test.
- luis: watch host memcpy perf and AMD/NVIDIA driver worker threads.

emily: Starting run A now. ping me in 25m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

arjun: Thanks — if A shows the issue consistently we will try B next.

perf-bot: disk usage warning on node infra-gpu-02: /var/tmp at 88%. Consider cleanup before long captures.

luis: I'll clean old traces in /var/tmp and bump retention policy.

emily: Run A finished. Uploading artifacts (nsys run_prefetch_03.qdrep, perfetto link soon).

emily: quick prelim: A p95 bumped from 12.1ms -> 20.4ms during sweep window. B (min_slice=4) reduced p95 to 13.3ms but dropped throughput ~2.6%. C (no prefetch) p95 12.8ms but throughput drop 4.1%. D (selector-delay + jitter) p95 12.5ms and throughput same as baseline.

maya: Excellent — D looks like the best tradeoff. Can we ship selector-delay=3ms default behind a feature flag?

arjun: Agree. Let's gate it behind `selector_delay_ms` feature flag and roll with canary.

emily: I'll open the rollout PR with telemetry (fallback-rate, p95, throughput) + server flag.

arjun: Great. Thanks everyone.
